title: Help
subtitle: Guided tours through each part of the dashboard.

basics.title: First steps
basics.body: Pages, edit mode, adding a widget, saving. The tour to run first.

widgets.title: Add and arrange widgets
widgets.body: Browse the catalog, link an entity, arrange tiles in panels and resize them.

panels.title: Build a modal
panels.body: In the launcher, “Modals” builds a sheet from blocks; a switch puts it in the left menu.

appearance.title: Look and wall panel
appearance.body: Dark or light theme, day/night switch, and the wall-tablet screensaver: large clock or photo frame.

floorplan.title: The Plan page
floorplan.body: The house in 3D: its chips, the security and thermal views, the day replay, and the model's settings.

events.title: Modals, toasts and notifications from Home Assistant
events.body: Fire an event from any automation to show a modal, a toast, or file a notification on every dashboard.

releaseNotes.title: What's new
releaseNotes.body: The changes brought by the latest version.

gestures.title: Swipe the screensaver
gestures.body: Change photo, open a quick menu or the notification drawer, without leaving the screensaver.

onboarding.title: Replay the welcome
onboarding.body: The welcome screens, and a new page built from your rooms.

events.intro: The dashboard listens for three custom events on the Home Assistant WebSocket. Any automation, script, or the Developer tools > Events tab can fire them — every open dashboard reacts at the same time. To try your own values: launcher > Developer tools.
events.modalDesc: A centred modal: title, text or HTML content, and action buttons that call a service.
events.toastDesc: A discreet notification in the corner, auto-dismissed unless made persistent.
events.demoModalBody: This is what an automation firing the ha_dashboard_modal event would display.
events.demoToastBody: Fired locally — no Home Assistant event involved.
events.tip: In Developer tools > Events, the type and the data are two separate fields: switch to "Dev tools" above to get the right shape. Pasting the whole "action:" block fires nothing.
events.notificationDesc: A notification that stays in the screensaver drawer (swipe down), surviving a reload, until it is dismissed.
events.demoNotificationBody: Filed in the drawer: swipe the screensaver down to find it.

gestures.intro: The screensaver is driven by touch. All four gestures below also work from the keyboard, with the arrow keys.

photos.title: Swipe left or right
photos.body: Next or previous slideshow photo. The timer restarts from scratch.

quick.title: Swipe up
quick.body: Opens the quick menu: one of your panels, picked in the WallPanel Gestures tab.

notifications.title: Swipe down
notifications.body: Opens the notification drawer. A pill at the top of the screen flags waiting messages.

exit.title: Tap once
exit.body: Leaves the screensaver. A swipe never leaves it, even though it ends with a tap.

gestures.config: Each gesture can be turned on or off separately in WallPanel > Gestures, along with the panel to open upwards.

devtools.title: Developer tools
devtools.subtitle: Try the events the dashboard listens to.
devtools.lockedDesc: Neither Escape nor a tap outside closes it: a button must be chosen.
devtools.sent: Sent: every open dashboard received it.
devtools.drawerHint: A notification doesn't pop up on screen: it lands in the screensaver's drawer (swipe down). Here is that drawer, as it stands.
devtools.soundOff: Sounds are turned off on this device: this event will stay silent here. Turn them on in Settings > Sound.

contentTypesDesc.plain: Shown as is, line breaks included.
contentTypesDesc.html: Read as HTML, sanitised before display.
contentTypesDesc.markdown: Shown as is: the dashboard doesn't format markdown.

devtools.dismissDesc: dismiss: true — removes a notification from the drawer.
devtools.dismissHint: With an identifier: removes that notification. Without one: clears the whole drawer.
devtools.lockedNoAction: With no button, nothing will close it: not Escape, not a tap outside. You will have to reload the page.
devtools.actionsDesc: As many as you like. A button with no label is ignored.
devtools.jsonInvalid: Invalid JSON: an object is expected, for example {"brightness_pct": 40}.
devtools.keepDesc: keep: true — the notification stays in the drawer once the button is pressed.

welcome.title: Welcome
welcome.body: Your home on one screen: lights, blinds, heating, music and cameras, at your fingertips. In two minutes we'll build your first page from your Home Assistant rooms.

look.title: Language and look
look.body: You can change these any time in Settings.
look.darkDesc: Easy on the eyes, ideal for an always-on wall tablet.
look.lightDesc: Bright and readable in a well-lit room.
look.autoDesc: Light by day, dark by night, following the sun.

rooms.title: Your rooms
rooms.body: Each ticked room gets a tile, and its lights, blinds, heating and players get a panel of their own. Rooms with nothing to control are unticked.
rooms.none: No rooms are set up in Home Assistant. We'll prepare a simple home page; you can add your devices afterwards.

ready.title: All set
ready.body: Your page is ready. Everything can be rearranged: the pencil at the top opens editing, the launcher leads to Settings and Help.
